title: Pitch Showmob to a skeptical developer in 90 seconds
summary: The pitch, the three objections you will actually get, and the one demo that settles it.

blocks.title: Ninety seconds, starting now
blocks.body: Your skeptic has heard every pitch and built half of them. Skip the vision deck. Here is the argument, in the order a developer actually hears it.

items.title: The claim
items.detail: Showmob is a visual language an AI can speak. Agents write JSON artifacts - one file per page - and a renderer draws them. No HTML generation, no layout hallucination, just a vocabulary of blocks.

items.title: Why that is not another page builder
items.detail: Page builders are editing surfaces for humans, tens of thousands of lines of drag-and-drop. Showmob is renderer-only. The authoring surface is the agent. The whole repo stays small enough for one agent to read end to end - that is the feature.

items.title: The mechanism
items.detail: Nineteen block types - hero, steps, timeline, comparison, exercise, and friends - with a runtime validator. Invalid JSON never renders. Themes are semantic tokens, so the agent picks a mood, not a hex code.

items.title: The proof
items.detail: A hundred artifacts were generated for grading night by four different generators, graded by a human reader. The grades train what good output looks like. Nobody else is measuring taste this way.

columns.name: 'JSON pages? I can prompt HTML directly'
columns.detail: And you get unreviewable, unvalidatable soup that drifts with the model. A constrained vocabulary is what makes output gradable, diffable, and safe to render untrusted.

columns.name: 'This is just a CMS'
columns.detail: A CMS serves pages to humans. Showmob serves pages written BY agents, and the grading loop is the point: the system learns which representation fits which situation. The CMS part is table stakes.

columns.name: 'Nineteen blocks will run out fast'
columns.detail: Correct, and deliberate. Blocks get added only when graded pages demand them - content, attempt, grade, then primitive. Never widget first, use case second.

blocks.heading: The close
blocks.body: Open the block gallery, then open any artifact's JSON. Thirty seconds of seeing both at once settles what ninety seconds of talking cannot: the agent writes meaning, and the renderer does the rest.
